blocks.text: Robot Wrap for Shopify: How We Re-Wrapped a Boston Dynamics Spot in Toronto

blocks.alt: Robot Wrap for Shopify: How We Re-Wrapped a Boston Dynamics Spot in Toronto

blocks.html:
Robot wrap projects don’t land on our table every day, so when Shopify asked us to re-skin their Boston Dynamics Spot robot, our team in Etobicoke jumped at it. This was a full robot wrap from the ground up: we stripped off the existing green digital-camo print, and re-wrapped every panel in a rich animal-fur finish before reassembling the unit. The result is a one-of-a-kind quadruped that turns heads at every Shopify event across Toronto and the GTA.

Here’s how we approached this custom object wrap — and what businesses anywhere in Ontario should know before wrapping something this unconventional.

Why Wrap a Robot at All?

A Boston Dynamics Spot isn’t a cheap piece of equipment, and Shopify uses theirs as a brand ambassador at conferences, demos, and media shoots. Vinyl gave them three things paint never could:

  • A reversible finish — the original shell stays protected and untouched underneath.
  • Brand flexibility — the look can change for a new campaign without buying new hardware.
  • Surface protection — the film shields the polycarbonate and ABS panels from scuffs and handling marks.

For high-value equipment like this, a custom object wrap is the smart, low-risk way to get a bold new identity. It’s the same logic behind our object and equipment wraps for everything from speaker boxes to welding masks.

The Process: From Green Camo to Fur

A robot is not a flat car panel. Spot is built from dozens of curved, jointed, and irregular components, so the only way to do this cleanly was to take it apart.

Step 1 — Disassembly

We carefully removed the individual panels, legs, and housings so each piece could be wrapped on the bench rather than on the assembled robot. This gives crisp wrapped edges with no lifting at the seams.

Step 2 — Removing the old print

The existing green-and-purple digital print was peeled off panel by panel. Clean removal matters — leftover adhesive ruins the next application. (We covered the right way to do this in our guide to safe vinyl unwrapping.)

Step 3 — Re-wrapping with the fur design

We printed and applied to each component, conforming the film over compound curves and tight contours.

Step 4 — Reassembly

Once every part was wrapped and laminated, we rebuilt Spot — back to fully functional, now wearing a completely new coat.

Materials We Used

For a printed wrap that lives on an expensive robot, material choice is everything. We used a premium 3M cast film and gloss laminate combination.

The 3M IJ180mC platform is rated for roughly 10 years of outdoor performance and is the same professional-grade film we use on full vehicle wraps. You can read more on 3M’s own graphics and vehicle film page, or see the colours and finishes we stock on our 3M and Avery Dennison materials page.

What Drives the Cost of an Object or Robot Wrap

Object wraps are priced differently than cars because complexity, not size, sets the labour. Here’s what affects the quote:

Small object wraps at our shop start around $150 CAD, while detailed custom-printed projects scale up from there. The honest answer for a unique piece like a robot is that it needs a look in person — which is exactly why we offer a free estimate.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Wrapping over a dirty or oily surface — adhesion fails fast.
  • Using cheap calendared vinyl on curves — it shrinks and lifts at the edges.
  • Skipping lamination on a printed wrap — the ink fades and scuffs without it.
  • Trying to wrap complex objects fully assembled — disassembly is what gives clean results.

These are the same fundamentals behind every great custom object wrap we produce.

Frequently Asked Questions

  1. Can you wrap a robot or other non-vehicle equipment?

    Yes. We wrap robots, machinery, appliances, signage, and almost any object that can take vinyl. Our object and equipment wrap service covers Etobicoke, Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan, and the wider GTA.

  2. Does a robot wrap damage the original surface?

    No. Quality cast film is removable and actually protects the shell underneath when applied and removed correctly.

  3. How long does a custom object wrap last?

    With 3M cast film and a gloss laminate, a printed wrap can last several years. Indoor equipment like an event robot typically lasts even longer since it avoids constant sun and weather.

  4. Why take the object apart instead of wrapping it whole?

    Disassembly lets us wrap each panel cleanly and tuck edges out of sight, which prevents lifting and gives a factory-finished look.

  5. Can you match my brand colours or create a custom design?

    Absolutely. Our in-house graphics team designs everything from solid brand colours to full photo-realistic prints like the fur finish on Spot.

  6. How much does a custom robot or object wrap cost in Toronto?

    It depends on size, number of parts, and design complexity. Small object wraps start near $150 CAD; custom-printed projects are quoted individually. We provide free estimates.

Ready to Wrap Something Unexpected?

From a Shopify robot to your company’s equipment, a professional robot wrap or custom object wrap transforms how your brand shows up — and our certified installers in Etobicoke make it look effortless. Serving Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan, and the entire GTA across Ontario, Canada.
